subject.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off `messages.strandedReplyRecovery` mode that replays normalized private `message_tool_only` final text into one synthetic retry prompt, or keep the strict no-message-call contract and pursue a different recovery policy?
rationale: Automation can review the code path, but it cannot choose the product and privacy contract for recovering private final text across channels, especially with an overlapping default-recovery successor PR open.

options.title: Accept opt-in recovery after proof
options.body: Keep the default false, require redacted real external channel proof, and let operators opt into one-shot recovery when they prefer recovery over strict silence.

options.title: Keep strict tool-only semantics
options.body: Reject the recovery surface and rely on stronger prompts, stronger models, or automatic visible replies for operators who cannot tolerate silence.

options.title: Choose a different recovery policy
options.body: Use the canonical issue or successor PR to sponsor another core or channel-owned policy, such as default recovery without a new config option.

recommendation.title: Accept opt-in recovery after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default false, require redacted real external channel proof, and let operators opt into one-shot recovery when they prefer recovery over strict silence.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the central auto-reply delivery/privacy boundary points to steipete through current blame and recent area work.
